map._comment: The generated map, the world played (#472, decision 0012): recipe (modules/world/data/maps/<recipe>.json) and seed, each overridden by --map= and --seed= (a missing or broken --map= falls back to this recipe); anything that falls kill_depth metres below the map's lowest ground (below 0 on the flat test world) is lost.

camp._comment: The players' camp (#420) on the map's camp pad (the recipe's settlements.camp.size): a square fence fence metres out from the pad's middle on every side, with a gate gate metres wide where the highway leaves. spots: where things stand inside it, in metres from the pad's middle, at [x, z] with x to the right as you face the gate and z toward the gate; toward [x, z] is the way each one faces (the board's and the stall's fronts, the hut's door; the cars' noses point the opposite way, so [0, -1] noses them at the gate; the players' car stands in line with the gate so it drives straight out). Players spawn and respawn at respawn; hut size is its floor [across, deep]. The tests hold every spot inside the fence and the fence on the pad; the pad must be at least 2 x (fence + 1) metres a side. Server and clients must have the same camp: each lays it out itself, nothing is sent.

roads._comment: How worn the map's roads are by how remote they are (0 by a settlement, 1 far from people, see the recipe's remoteness): wear and potholes go from [0] at 0 to [1] at 1 (what generation starts with; damage players do stays).

water._comment: How ponds look (the map recipe places them): shallow and deep water colours [r, g, b] and colour_depth (metres to fully deep), shore_colour within shore_depth metres of the bank, sky (the reflected colour), wind [x, z] (ripple direction and strength), ripple_speed and ripple_seconds. sea: the sea round an island map (#454), the same fields for its own look (what it leaves out is as a pond's), plus wave_scale (under 1 makes the wave pattern larger), wave_strength (how much the crests stand out), foam [r, g, b], foam_depth (metres of water at the shore that foam runs in over, 0 for none) and foam_speed, bed [r, g, b] (the sea floor as seen through the water past bed_distance metres, where the ground drawn under it is coarse or not there); depth_limit: metres of sea under a swimmer past which they tire (modules/player/data/player.json sea_stamina_seconds), so the sea, not a wall, is the world's edge.

ground._comment: How the visible voxel ground is drawn (#498, decision 0015; drawing only, collision is the smooth ground either way). tilt_grade: a column on ground gentler than this (rise over run) tilts its top to the true height; steeper ground keeps flat steps. band: metres past a road's or track's edge (its earthworks shoulder included) where the ground tilts to meet the strip, and pad_band past a levelled pad's (a site's, a town's), unless steeper than band_grade (a steep bank keeps its steps). ledge: on ground at least ledge_grade steep, clear of those bands, steps are this many metres tall (whole voxels, rounded to the nearest ledge; no finer than a voxel), so a steep slope reads as rock ledges; keep ledge_grade no lower than the scatter's max_steepness, so no tree or rock stands where a ledge may bury its foot. wall_light: the share of the sun's light that step sides facing away from it get, bounced off the lit ground, so they stay their colour in shade. tilt_variation: per-voxel brightness variation on tilted tops (flat tops have 0.07). track_fray: metres the ground's ragged edge comes in over a dirt track's strip (near tiles draw it a few millimetres over the strip); track_verge: share of the cells just past its edge drawn as a verge. yard_fray: metres a yard's edge wanders out, yard_round: how round its corners are (metres). Lanes (site yards) are painted into the ground: lane_soil [r, g, b], toned lane_mix of the way toward the ground under it; verge_mix: a verge cell's colour lies that far from the soil toward the ground; rut_dark: how much darker a lane's wheel ruts are (as a track strip's worn ruts).

scatter._comment: Trees, rocks and grass (TWEAKING.md lists the rest). site_clearance: metres round each map site's pad, by site kind, kept free of trees and rocks so they don't crowd what stands there; default for kinds not listed. power_clearance: metres either side of a high-voltage line and of a pole line (at most 32) kept free of trees and rocks, so no crown grows into the wires. camp_clearance: metres round the players' camp pad kept free of trees and rocks. max_steepness: no tree or rock on ground steeper than this (rise over run); grass_max_steepness: no grass on ground steeper than this, which the ground draws in ledges (keep both at or under ground.ledge_grade). build_budget_ms: milliseconds a frame may spend putting new scenery chunks together (collision, grass, road pieces); the rest waits for the next frame.
